chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whenever one of you eats food, let him lick the fingers with which he ate.'
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Allah will bless you in it.'

key_terms.بَارَكَ اللَّهُ فِيكَ: Allah will bless you in it

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic etiquette for eating regarding one's fingers?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the Prophetic etiquette of licking fingers to avoid wasting food, linking physical mindfulness to divine blessing. In Shia tradition, this act is viewed not merely as hygiene but as an expression of gratitude (shukr) for Allah's provisions, reinforcing the spiritual value of everyday actions. The promise of 'barakah' (blessing) in the food underscores the connection between mindful consumption and spiritual sustenance.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Whenever one of you eats food, so he should lick the fingers which he ate with’.
Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Said: “Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Bless you in it”’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Qasim ibn Yahya from his grandfather al-Hassan ibn Rashid from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has stated this Hadith.

‘The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, “When one of you eats food he should wipe (lick) his fingers, clean with which he has eaten;
Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, says, ‘Allah grants you blessings.”””
